issues.title: Missing principal-part scaling in the CAP form
issues.failure_explanation: Integrating the displayed CAP equation by parts yields the principal term \(\int_\Omega k^{-2}(A_{\rm scat}\nabla u)\cdot\overline{\nabla v}\). The old equation instead uses coefficient one. Consequently it is neither the weak form of eq:CAP nor of the abstract form based on the \(H_k^1\) inner product in eq:1kip.
issues.overall_effect: The interface between the CAP PDE, its Galerkin matrix, and the abstract normalized Helmholtz analysis is inconsistent as printed, so the CAP-specific application chain requires the correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor k^{-2} in front of the principal term in eq:sesqui_CAP, and use that corrected form when defining the CAP Galerkin matrix and invoking the listed CAP applications. No hypotheses, conclusions, rates, or dependent proofs otherwise need to change.
issues.why_classification: Both eq:CAP and the H_k^1 inner product in eq:1kip uniquely force the factor k^{-2}, and the subsequent abstract analysis consistently uses that normalization. Restoring the omitted factor is a uniquely determined transcriptional correction with no mathematical loss or new inference.

issues.title: Interpolated coarse generators need not be independent
issues.failure_explanation: Case (b) claims the original coarse-space dimension and a matrix preconditioner after setting \(\mathcal V_0=\mathcal I_h\widetilde{\mathcal V}_0\). The assumptions do not make \(\mathcal I_h\) injective on \(\widetilde{\mathcal V}_0\). For example, with \(p_f=1\), \(p_c=3\), and a coarse triangle split into four fine triangles through its edge midpoints, the cubic bubble on an interior coarse element vanishes at every fine P1 node and is mapped to zero. This nested configuration is admissible after scaling the mesh to meet the stated smallness conditions. Hence the interpolated generators can be dependent, the claimed dimension need not be the original coarse dimension, and the displayed \(R_0AR_0^T\) can be singular.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract theorem for the image space may remain valid if an actual basis of that image is chosen, but the Case (b) dimension claim and the advertised matrix realization using every original coarse generator are not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the coarse space as the image I_h applied to the original coarse space, but use a rank-revealing factorization to replace the possibly redundant interpolated generators by an actual basis of that image before defining R_0 and A_0. State the dimension as the rank of the interpolation map. For fixed p_f and p_c, the inclusion of the nested coarse degree-p_f space in the image, together with containment in the original degree-p_c space, gives the same asymptotic dimension scaling. Lemma lem:firstclass and Theorem thm:repQ then apply to the genuine basis.
issues.why_classification: The literal generator family can be dependent, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, ordinary finite-dimensional basis extraction and an elementary dimension sandwich repair the matrix realization while preserving the image space, approximation result, GMRES guarantee, and advertised asymptotic coarse-dimension rate. No new analytic argument or meaningful mathematical loss is required.

issues.title: Wrong exponent in the CAP lower-order coefficient

failure_location.quote: Observe that the sesquilinear form of the CAP problem of Definition \ref{def:CAP} satisfies Assumption \ref{ass:sesqui} with $\coefflower := (-c_{\rm scat}^2 - \ri V - 1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the CAP form satisfies ass:sesqui with \(\mu=-c_{\rm scat}^{2}-iV-1\). The old displayed CAP form actually has zeroth-order coefficient \(-c_{\rm scat}^{-2}-iV\), and subtracting the \(+1\) contributed by the \(H_k^1\) inner product requires \(\mu=-c_{\rm scat}^{-2}-iV-1\). The material mismatch is the square versus inverse-square dependence on \(c_{\rm scat}\).
issues.overall_effect: The prose gives the wrong exact embedding coefficient, although the displayed CAP coefficient itself makes the intended correction immediate and the qualitative boundedness assumptions are unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace −c_scat^{2} by −c_scat^{-2} in the stated value of the lower-order coefficient, so that μ=−c_scat^{-2}−iV−1.
issues.why_classification: The inverse-square coefficient is uniquely forced by the displayed CAP form and by subtracting the +1 term in the H_k^1 inner product. This is a one-symbol transcription error; the boundedness assumptions and every qualitative guarantee remain unchanged.

issues.title: Undefined local-space definition at index zero
issues.failure_explanation: The old definition requires \(\mathcal V_0=\mathcal V_h\cap H_0^1(\Omega_0)\), but no \(\Omega_0\) exists and the independently declared \(\mathcal V_0\) is the coarse space. Thus the displayed family defining the operators has an undefined and conflicting index-zero interface.
issues.overall_effect: The literal definition of \(Q_0\) is malformed, although the immediately following coarse-space assumption makes the intended reading unambiguous and later arguments consistently use that reading.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the local spaces V_ell=V_h∩H_0^1(Omega_ell) only for ell=1,…,N, and retain the independently defined coarse space as V_0 and the range of Q_0.
issues.why_classification: No Omega_0 is defined, while the immediately following coarse-space assumption and all later uses uniquely identify V_0 with the coarse space. Changing the erroneous index range is a purely transcriptional correction and requires no change to the construction or analysis.

issues.title: Truncation destroys the exact stable decomposition
issues.failure_explanation: The lemma requires the exact identity \(v_h=\sum_\ell v_{h,\ell}\). The proof first has \(\sum_\ell\widetilde v_{h,\ell}=v_h\), but its final definition gives \(\sum_\ell v_{h,\ell}=v_h-\sum_\ell\mathcal I_h(\psi_\ell\widetilde v_{h,\ell})\). No cancellation or vanishing of this correction is proved; exponential smallness near subdomain boundaries would not imply the exact equality required by the statement.
issues.overall_effect: The degree-explicit stable splitting and the abstract field-of-values chain based on it are not established. The fixed-degree application using lem:split_old is not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the truncated global projection by the linear projection P_hp from Vo:25, Section 3, as stated in v4's theorem t:QIV. Its reproduction property is cited at equation (3.9), and its degree-independent local gradient and L^2 approximation bounds at equations (3.14) and (3.15). Set v_(h,ell)=P_hp(chi_ell v_h). Linearity, reproduction, and sum_ell chi_ell=1 give exact reconstruction. For support, explicitly require each projector patch associated with an element outside Omega_ell to miss supp chi_ell; align the existing geometric support buffer with these two-neighbour patches. Then the local L^2 approximation bound shows v_(h,ell)=0 outside Omega_ell. Prove the splitting bound C(1+kh)^2 Lambda [||v_h||_(H^1_k)^2+(k delta)^(-2)||v_h||_(L^2)^2], using the local approximation bounds, product rule, bounded patch overlap, and partition-of-unity gradient bound. Do not replace these estimates by an unsupported assertion of simultaneous degree-uniform L^2 and H^1 stability. In the bounded-kh regime of the old downstream application, this estimate is at least as strong as the required p_f^2 bound, whose extra E^2 term is nonnegative. Use it in lem:key_Garding and the recorded field-of-values chain. For standalone statements outside that regime, carry the explicit (1+kh)^2 dependence rather than asserting the old parameter-uniform estimate verbatim. The wider v4 coarse-space and complexity revisions are not all consequences of this root.
issues.why_classification: Exponential smallness cannot restore the exact decomposition identity lost by truncation. The concrete projector route restores it, but verifying the patch support condition and degree-explicit estimates is contained nontrivial work. The resulting bound restores the splitting input in the checked bounded-kh downstream regime, without global reconstruction or major loss there. Moderate is justified by that complete contained route; it is not a claim that every old standalone parameter regime or every theorem in the authors' wider revision is unchanged.

issues.title: Stable-splitting proof uses an excluded interpolation endpoint
issues.failure_explanation: The estimate eq:hope3 is introduced with “Theorem thm:interpolationMS1 with \(m=1\),” but that theorem is stated only for \(m\geq2\). The resulting \(h/p_f\) L2 estimate supplies the degree dependence needed for eq:hope1 and ultimately the \(p_f^2\) splitting bound. Merely applying the stated \(m=2\) result does not establish the same dependence, so the proof uses a result outside its stated hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: Independently of the exact-decomposition failure, the degree-explicit stability estimate needed by the main abstract chain is unsupported. The fixed-degree chain using lem:split_old is unaffected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid m=1 invocation by a proved p-optimal quasi-interpolation estimate. Concretely, use an H^1-stable map J_h into V_h satisfying ||w−J_h w||_{L^2}≤C(h/p_f)||w||_{H^1}. Comparing the L^2 projection with J_h and applying the finite-element inverse estimate gives |Pi_h^{L^2}w|_{H^1}≤Cp_f||w||_{H^1} for the products used in the proof, which supplies eq:hope1 without invoking thm:interpolationMS1 outside its hypotheses. The remaining stable-splitting and dependent arguments can then proceed with the claimed p_f-dependence.
issues.why_classification: The endpoint is genuinely absent from the stated theorem, and the required h/p_f dependence cannot be recovered by merely substituting m=2. Establishing it requires a separate degree-explicit quasi-interpolation result and a contained replacement argument. That work is nontrivial but local to the stability estimate and preserves the affected chain, so the issue is moderate.

issues.title: Free frequency threshold in the CAP approximation theorem

failure_location.quote: Then, given $s, M>0$ and $\chi \in C^\infty_{\rm comp}(\Omega_{\rm int})$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem chooses its constant after specifying \(s\), \(M\), and \(\chi\), but then states the estimate for all \(k\geq k_0\) even though no \(k_0\) has been selected or quantified in that theorem. The intended uniform statement becomes well formed only after prescribing \(k_0>0\) before choosing the constant.
issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary CAP approximation theorem has an incomplete quantifier contract. The paper expressly says this theorem is not used in the subsequent preconditioner analysis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Quantify the threshold before the constant: given k_0>0, s,M>0, and χ, there exists C (allowed to depend on k_0) such that the estimate holds for every k≥k_0.
issues.why_classification: The occurrence of the otherwise free k_0 makes the statement syntactically incomplete, and the surrounding high-frequency formulation uniquely indicates that k_0 is a prescribed positive threshold. No proof or substantive guarantee changes.

issues.title: Elman estimate applied to an unshifted Krylov iteration
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:rm puts \(x^m\) in \(\mathcal K^m(C,r^0)\), not in \(x^0+\mathcal K^m(C,r^0)\). The failure is internally checkable: take \(C=I_2\), \(D=I_2\), \(d=e_1\), and \(x^0=e_2\). Then \(r^0=e_1-e_2\), every stated Krylov space is its one-dimensional span, and minimizing \(\|e_1-x\|\) over that span leaves a nonzero residual. But \(W(C)=\{1\}\), so thm:Elman has \(\beta=0\), \(\gamma_\beta=0\), and asserts zero residual after one step. The theorem is therefore being applied to an invalid iteration.
issues.overall_effect: The stated weighted-GMRES convergence chain is false for a general nonzero initial iterate. It remains valid in the special case \(x^0=0\), where the affine and linear spaces coincide.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct eq:rm to affine GMRES: minimize over x^0+K^m(C,r^0), equivalently write x^m=x^0+z^m with z^m in K^m(C,r^0) minimizing ||r^0−Cz^m||_D. Apply thm:Elman and all listed corollaries to this standard affine iteration.
issues.why_classification: The displayed linear-space iteration is a coherent but incorrect algorithm for nonzero x^0, so the Elman inference is invalid as written and the defect is more than a transcriptional typo. The standard affine correction is nevertheless short and routine, requires no new lemma, and preserves the arbitrary-initial-iterate convergence mode, rate, and all downstream guarantees.
